7.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.1.text: The Bhagavat said, "O son of Prtha, hear from Me how, with your mind attached to Me, practicing yoga, and taking refuge in Me, you shall understand Me fully, without any doubt."

7.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.1.text: The Lord said, "With your mind focused on Me, taking Me as your support, and practicing yoga—how can you, without doubt, know Me fully? Hear, O Arjuna."

7.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.1.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O Partha, hear how, with your mind fixed on Me, practicing the Yoga of Meditation and taking refuge in Me, you will certainly and fully know Me.

7.1.author: Swami Sivananda
7.1.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, hear how you shall, without doubt, know Me fully, with your mind intent on Me, practicing Yoga and taking refuge in Me."

7.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.1.text: Lord Shri Krishna said: Listen, O Arjuna! I will tell you how you can know Me in my full perfection. Practice meditation with your mind devoted to Me and take Me as your refuge.

7.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.2.text: I shall teach you this knowledge in full, together with action; for a person who has known this, there remains nothing else to be known in this world.

7.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.2.text: I will declare to you in full this knowledge of God, along with the knowledge that makes it distinguished, knowing which nothing else remains to be known.

7.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.2.text: I shall tell you in detail of this Knowledge, which is combined with realization, after experiencing which there remains nothing else here to be known.

7.2.author: Swami Sivananda
7.2.text: I will declare to you in full this knowledge combined with realization, after knowing which nothing else remains to be known here.

7.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.2.text: I will reveal this knowledge to you and how it can be realized; once accomplished, there is nothing else worth having in this life.

7.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.3.text: Among thousands of men, perhaps one makes an effort for the determined knowledge. Among those, even though they make an effort, perhaps one realizes Me correctly with the determined knowledge.

7.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.3.text: Among thousands of men, some strive for perfection; even among those who strive for perfection, only some know Me; and among those who know Me, only some truly know Me.

7.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.3.text: Among thousands of men, a rare one endeavors for perfection. Even among the perfected ones who are diligent, one perchance knows Me in truth.

7.3.author: Swami Sivananda
7.3.text: Among thousands of men, one may perchance strive for perfection; even among those successful strivers, only one may perchance know Me in essence.

7.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.3.text: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection, and even among those who gain occult powers, perhaps only one knows me in truth.

7.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.4.text: My nature is divided into eight parts: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Ether, Mind, Intellect, and Ego.

7.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.4.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, Manas, Buddhi, and the ego-sense—thus My Prakriti is divided into eight parts.

7.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.4.text: This Prakrti of Mine is divided eightfold thus: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and egoism.

7.4.author: Swami Sivananda
7.4.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and egoism—thus is My Nature divided eightfold.

7.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.4.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and personality—this is the eightfold division of My manifested nature.

7.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.5.text: This is My lower nature. My superior nature, which has become the individual Soul and by which this world is maintained, is not different from this. O mighty-armed Arjuna, you must know this.

7.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.5.text: This is My lower Prakṛti. But, O mighty-armed one, know that My higher nature is another. It is the life-principle (Jīva-bhūta), by which this universe is sustained.

7.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.5.text: O mighty-armed one, this is the inferior Prakrti. Know the other Prakrti of Mine, which is however higher than this, which has taken the form of individual souls, and by which this world is upheld.

7.5.author: Swami Sivananda
7.5.text: O mighty-armed Arjuna, this is the inferior Prakriti; know it as distinct from My higher Prakriti, the very life-element, by which this world is upheld.

7.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.5.text: This is My inferior nature; however, O valiant one, know that distinct from this is My superior nature, which is the very life that sustains the universe.

7.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.6.text: All beings are born from this womb; hence, keep them close. I am the origin and dissolution of the entire world.

7.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.6.text: Know that all beings have these two as the source of their birth. Therefore, I am the origin and the dissolver of the whole universe.

7.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.6.text: Understand thus that all things—sentient and insentient—have these as their source. I am the origin as well as the end of the entire universe.

7.6.author: Swami Sivananda
7.6.text: Know that these two are the womb of all beings; thus, I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.

7.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.6.text: It is the womb of all beings; for I am He by Whom the worlds were created and shall be dissolved.

7.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.7.text: There is nothing beyond Me, O Dhananjaya; all this is strung on Me, just as pearls are strung on a string.

7.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.7.text: There is nothing higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, like rows of gems on a thread.

7.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.7.text: O Dhananjaya, there is nothing else higher than Myself. All this is strung on Me like pearls on a string.

7.7.author: Swami Sivananda
7.7.text: There is nothing higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, like clusters of gems on a string.

7.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.7.text: O Arjuna! There is nothing higher than Me; all is strung on Me like rows of pearls on a thread.

7.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.8.text: O son of Kunti! I am the taste in waters, the light in the moon and sun, the best hymn (OM) in the entire Vedas, the sound that exists in the ether, and the manly vigor in men.

7.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.8.text: I am the taste in the waters, O Arjuna! I am the light in the sun and the moon; the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas; sound in the ether; and manhood in men, I am.

7.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.8.text: O son of Kunti, I am the taste of water, I am the effulgence of the moon and the sun; the letter 'Om' in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and manhood in men.

7.8.author: Swami Sivananda
7.8.text: I am the flavor in water, O Arjuna; I am the light in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in the ether and virility in men.

7.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.8.text: O Arjuna! I am the fluidity in water, the light in the sun and moon, the mystic syllable Om in the Vedic scriptures, the sound in ether, and the virility in man.

7.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.9.text: I am the pure scent in the earth; I am also the radiance in the sun; I am the life in all beings and the austerity in the ascetics.

7.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.9.text: I am the pure scent in the earth; I am the radiance in the fire; I am the life-force in all beings, and austerity in ascetics.

7.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.9.text: I am also the sweet fragrance in the earth; I am the brilliance in the fire, and the life in all beings; and I am the austerity of the ascetics.

7.9.author: Swami Sivananda
7.9.text: I am the sweet fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in the fire, the life in all beings, and I am the austerity of ascetics.

7.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.9.text: I am the fragrance of the earth, the brilliance of fire, the life force in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics.

7.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.10.text: O son of Prtha! Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intellect of the intellectuals and the brilliance of the brilliant.

7.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.10.text: Know Me, O Arjuna, to be the primeval seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the discerning and the brilliance of the brilliant.

7.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.10.text: O Partha, know Me to be the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intellect of the intelligent, and I am the courage of the courageous.

7.10.author: Swami Sivananda
7.10.text: Know Me, O Arjuna, as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intelligence of the intelligent, and the splendour of the splendid objects.

7.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.10.text: Know, O Arjuna, that I am the eternal seed of being; I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendour of the resplendent.

7.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.11.text: Of the strong, I am the strength that is free from desire and attachment. O best of the Bharatas, in all beings, I am the desire that is not contrary to dharma.

7.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.11.text: In the strong, I am strength, devoid of desire and passion. In all beings, I am the desire which is not contrary to Dharma, O Arjuna.

7.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.11.text: And of the strong, I am the strength that is devoid of passion and attachment. Among creatures, I am desire that is not contrary to righteousness, O scion of the Bharata dynasty.

7.11.author: Swami Sivananda
7.11.text: Of the strong, I am the strength devoid of desire and attachment, and in all beings, I am the desire in accordance with Dharma, O Arjuna.

7.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.11.text: I am the strength of the strong, those who are free from attachment and desire; and, O Arjuna, I am the desire for righteousness.

7.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.12.text: Whatever beings are there—whether they are of the Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas strands—be sure that they are from Me; I am not in them, but they are within Me.

7.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.12.text: Know that all those states of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas are from Me alone; however, I am not in them; rather, they are in Me.

7.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.12.text: Those things that are made of the quality of sattva, and those things that are made of the quality of rajas and tamas, know them to have sprung from Me alone. However, I am not in them; they are within Me!

7.12.author: Swami Sivananda
7.12.text: Whatever beings (and objects) that are pure, active, and inert, know that they proceed from Me. They are in Me, yet I am not in them.

7.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.12.text: Whatever be the nature of their life, whether it be pure, passionate, or ignorant, they are all derived from Me. They are in Me, but I am not in them.

7.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.13.text: Being deluded by these three strands of nature, this entire world does not recognize Me, who am eternal and transcend these strands.

7.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.13.text: The entire universe is deluded by these three states originating from the Gunas (of Prakrti), and fails to recognize Me, who am beyond them and immutable.

7.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.13.text: All this world, deluded as it is by these three qualities made of the gunas, does not know Me, who am transcendental to these and undecaying.

7.13.author: Swami Sivananda
7.13.text: Deluded by these Natures, composed of the three qualities of Nature, all this world does not know Me as distinct from them and immutable.

7.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.13.text: The inhabitants of the world, misled by the natures engendered by the Qualities, do not know that I am higher than them all and that I do not change.

7.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.14.text: This is My divine play, composed of the strands of illusion, and it is hard to cross over. Those who take refuge in Me alone, they cross over the illusion.

7.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.14.text: For this divine Maya or Mine, consisting of the three Gunas (assumed for purposes of sport), is hard to overcome. But those who take refuge in Me alone shall pass beyond the Maya.

7.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.14.text: Since this divine Maya of Mine, which is constituted by the gunas, is difficult to cross over, those who take refuge in Me alone can transcend this Maya.

7.14.author: Swami Sivananda
7.14.text: Verily, this divine illusion of Mine, composed of the three qualities, is difficult to cross over; those who take refuge in Me alone, can cross over this illusion.

7.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.14.text: Verily, this divine illusion of phenomenon manifesting itself in the qualities is difficult to surmount. Only they who devote themselves exclusively to Me can accomplish it.

7.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.15.text: The deluded evil-doers, the vilest of men, who are robbed of knowledge by the trick of illusion and have taken refuge in the demonic nature—they do not resort to Me.

7.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.15.text: The evil-doers, the foolish, the lowest of men, those persons deprived of knowledge by delusion (Maya) and those who are dominated by a demoniac nature - they do not seek refuge in Me.

7.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.15.text: The foolish evildoers, who are the most depraved among men, who are deprived of their wisdom by Maya, and who resort to demonic ways, do not take refuge in Me.

7.15.author: Swami Sivananda
7.15.text: The evil-doers and the deluded, who are the lowest of men, do not seek Me; those whose knowledge is destroyed by illusion follow the ways of demons.

7.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.15.text: The sinner, the ignorant, the vile, deprived of spiritual perception by the glamour of illusion, and he who leads a godless life—none of them shall find me.

7.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.16.text: Men of good action who always worship Me are of four types: the afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of wisdom, O best among the Bharatas!

7.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.16.text: Four types of men of good deeds worship Me, O Arjuna: the distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the men of knowledge.

7.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.16.text: O Arjuna, foremost of the Bharata dynasty, four classes of people of virtuous deeds adore Me: the afflicted, the seekers of Knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the man of Knowledge.

7.16.author: Swami Sivananda
7.16.text: Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna, and they are the distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the wise, O Lord of the Bharatas.

7.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.16.text: O Arjuna! The righteous who worship Me are grouped in stages: first, those who suffer, next those who desire knowledge, then those who thirst after truth, and lastly those who attain wisdom.

7.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.17.text: Of them, the man of wisdom, being always attached to Me with single-pointed devotion, excels. For, I am dear to the man of wisdom above all personal gains, and he is dear to Me.

7.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.17.text: Of these, the man of knowledge, who is ever with Me in Yoga and devoted to the One only, is the foremost; for I am very dear to the man of knowledge, and he is also dear to Me.

7.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.17.text: Of them, the man of knowledge, endowed with constant steadfastness and one-pointed devotion, excels. For I am very dear to the man of knowledge, and he too is dear to me.

7.17.author: Swami Sivananda
7.17.text: Of them, the wise who are ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excel; for I am exceedingly dear to the wise, and they are dear to Me.

7.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.17.text: Of all these, he who has gained wisdom, who meditates on Me without ceasing, devoting himself solely to Me, is the best; for I am exceedingly beloved by the wise man, and the wise man is also beloved by Me.

7.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.18.text: All these are indeed noble persons. But the man of wisdom is considered as the very Soul of Mine. For, with his self (mind) that has mastered the Yoga, he has resorted to Me alone as his most supreme goal.

7.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.18.text: All these are indeed generous, but I deem the man of knowledge to be My very self; for he, integrated, is devoted solely to Me as the highest end.

7.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.18.text: Indeed, all of these are noble, but the man of Knowledge is the Self itself. This is my opinion. For, with a steadfast mind, he is set on the path leading only to Me, who am the supreme Goal.

7.18.author: Swami Sivananda
7.18.text: Indeed, all these are noble; however, I consider the wise man as My very Self; for, he is steadfast in mind and established in Me alone as the supreme goal.

7.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.18.text: Noble-minded are they all, but the wise man I hold as my own self; for he, remaining always at peace with me, makes me his ultimate goal.

7.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.19.text: At the end of many births, one attains Me with the conviction that 'All is Vasudeva'- that noble soul is very difficult to attain.

7.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.19.text: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge finds refuge in Me, realizing that 'Vasudeva is all.' It is very difficult to find such a great-souled person.

7.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.19.text: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge attains Me, realizing that Vasudeva is all. Such a high-souled one is very rare.

7.19.author: Swami Sivananda
7.19.text: At the end of many births, the wise man comes to Me, realizing that all this is Vaasudeva (the innermost Self); such a great soul (Mahatma) is very hard to find.

7.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.19.text: After many lives, at last the wise one realizes Me as I am. It is very difficult to find a man so enlightened that he sees God everywhere.

7.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.20.text: Being robbed of their wisdom by innumerable desires and controlled by their own nature, persons take refuge in other deities, following one or the other religious regulations.

7.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.20.text: Controlled by their inherent nature, and deprived of knowledge by various desires, worldly-minded people resort to other gods, observing various disciplines.

7.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.20.text: People, deprived of their wisdom by desires for various objects and guided by their own nature, resort to other deities, following the relevant methods.

7.20.author: Swami Sivananda
7.20.text: Those whose wisdom has been taken away by this or that desire, go to other gods, following this or that rite, led by their own nature.

7.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.20.text: They in whom wisdom is obscured by one desire or another, worship the lesser powers, practicing many rites that vary according to their temperaments.

7.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.21.text: Whatever form of deity a devotee, whomever they may be, desires to worship with faith, I assume that form which is firm and is according to their faith.

7.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.21.text: Whichever devotee seeks to worship with faith whatever form, I make their faith steadfast.

7.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.21.text: Whichever form of a deity any devotee wants to worship with faith, I strengthen that very firm faith of theirs.

7.21.author: Swami Sivananda
7.21.text: Whatever form any devotee desires to worship with faith, I make that same faith of his firm and unflinching.

7.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.21.text: But whatever form of worship, if the devotee has faith, then I set My own seal upon their faith in that worship.

7.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.22.text: Endowed with that faith, he seeks to worship that deity and thereby receives his desired objects, which are ordained by none other than Me.

7.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.22.text: Endowed with that faith, he worships that form and thereby gets the objects of his desire, granted in reality by Me alone.

7.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.22.text: Being imbued with that faith, that person engages in worshipping that form, and they get those very desired results as dispensed by Me alone.

7.22.author: Swami Sivananda
7.22.text: Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that form and obtains his desired outcome, which is ordained by Me alone.

7.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.22.text: If he worships one form alone with real faith, then his desires shall be fulfilled through that alone; for thus I have ordained.

7.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.23.text: But the fruit of those of poor intellect is finite; those who perform sacrifices aiming at the gods go to the gods, and My devotees come to Me.

7.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.23.text: But the fruit gained by these men of small understanding is limited. The worshippers of the gods will go to the gods, but My devotees will come to Me.

7.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.23.text: The result of those who are of poor intellect is indeed limited. The worshippers of gods go to the gods, while My devotees go to Me alone.

7.23.author: Swami Sivananda
7.23.text: Verily, the reward (fruit) that accrues to those men of small intelligence is finite. The worshippers of the gods go to them, whereas My devotees come to Me.

7.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.23.text: The fruit that comes to people of limited insight is, after all, finite. Those who worship the Lower Powers attain them; but those who worship Me come to Me alone.

7.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.24.text: Those of poor intellect are not aware of My higher, unchanging, and supreme nature; and thus, they consider Me, the Unmanifest, to be manifest.

7.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.24.text: Not knowing My higher, immutable, and unsurpassed nature, the ignorant think of Me as an entity that has now become manifest, though I was previously unmanifest.

7.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.24.text: The unintelligent, unaware of My supreme state which is immutable and unsurpassable, think of Me as having become manifest from the unmanifest.

7.24.author: Swami Sivananda
7.24.text: The foolish think of Me, the Unmanifest, as having manifestation, not knowing My higher, immutable, and most excellent nature.

7.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.24.text: The ignorant think of Me, who am the Unmanifested Spirit, as if I were in human form. They do not understand that My Superior Nature is unchanging and most excellent.

7.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.25.text: Being surrounded by the trick of yoga-illusion, I am not clear to all; hence, this deluded world of perceivers does not recognize Me, the unborn and undying.

7.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.25.text: Veiled by my Maya, I am not manifest to all; this deluded world does not recognize me as the unborn and immutable.

7.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.25.text: Being enveloped by yoga-maya, I do not become manifest to all. This deluded world does not know Me, who am birthless and undecaying.

7.25.author: Swami Sivananda
7.25.text: I am not manifest to all, veiled as I am by the Yoga-Maya. This deluded world does not know Me, who am unborn and imperishable.

7.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.25.text: I am not visible to all, for I am enveloped by the illusion of the Phenomenon. This deluded world does not know Me as the Unborn and Imperishable.

7.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.26.text: O Arjuna, I know the beings that have gone, that are present, and those yet to be born; but no one knows Me.

7.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.26.text: I know all beings, O Arjuna, past, present, and those to come; but no one knows Me.

7.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.26.text: O Arjuna, I know the past, present, and future beings; but no one knows Me!

7.26.author: Swami Sivananda
7.26.text: I know, O Arjuna, the beings of the past, the present, and the future; however, no one knows Me.

7.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.26.text: I know, O Arjuna, all beings in the past, the present, and the future; but they do not know Me.

7.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.27.text: O descendant of Bharata, O scorcher of foes! At the time of creation, all beings become deluded due to the illusion of pairs of opposites arising from desire and hatred.

7.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.27.text: O Arjuna, all beings are deluded as soon as they are born, due to the delusion of the pairs of opposites springing from desire and hate.

7.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.27.text: O scion of the Bharata dynasty, O destroyer of foes, due to the delusion of duality arising from likes and dislikes, all creatures become bewildered upon their birth.

7.27.author: Swami Sivananda
7.27.text: O Bharata, all beings are subject to delusion at birth due to the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O Parantapa.

7.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.27.text: O brave Arjuna! Man lives in a fantastical world, deceived by the glamour of opposing sensations, infatuated by desire and aversion.

7.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.28.text: But those men of virtuous deeds, whose sin has come to an end—they, being free from the delusion of pairs [of opposites], worship Me with a firm resolve.

7.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.28.text: But those who have done good deeds, whose sins have come to an end, are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites. They steadfastly worship Me, adhering to their vows.

7.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.28.text: On the other hand, those persons who have done virtuous deeds, whose sin has come to an end, they, being free from the delusion of duality and firm in their convictions, adore Me.

7.28.author: Swami Sivananda
7.28.text: But those men of virtuous deeds, whose sins have come to an end and who are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me steadfastly, with their vows.

7.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.28.text: But those who act righteously, in whom sin has been destroyed, who are free from the infatuation of conflicting emotions, they worship Me with a firm resolve.

7.29.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.29.text: Those who, relying on Me, strive to achieve freedom from old age and death, realize all to be the Brahman and realize all the actions governing the Self.

7.29.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.29.text: Those who take refuge in Me and strive for deliverance from old age and death, know Brahman (or the Self) and all about the nature of that Self, and the entire Karma (or activities leading to rebirth).

7.29.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.29.text: Those who strive by resorting to Me for becoming free from old age and death, they know Brahman, the individual Self, and all about actions. [They know Brahman as being all the individual entities and all actions. This verse prescribes meditation on the qualified Brahman for aspirants of the middle class. Verses beginning with the 14th speak about the realization of the unqualified Brahman by aspirants of the highest class.]

7.29.author: Swami Sivananda
7.29.text: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me, realize in full that Brahman, the whole knowledge of the Self, and all action.

7.29.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.29.text: Those who make Me their refuge, striving for liberation from decay and death, realize the Supreme Spirit, which is their own real Self, and in which all action finds its consummation.

7.30.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
7.30.text: Those who realize Me as one [identical] with what governs the beings, deities, and with what governs the sacrifices—they, even at the moment of their departure, experience Me, having mastered the Yoga.

7.30.author: Swami Adidevananda
7.30.text: And those who know Me with the Adhibhuta, Adhidaiva, and Adhiyajna, they too, with their minds fixed in meditation, know Me even at the hour of death.

7.30.author: Swami Gambirananda
7.30.text: Those who know me as existing in both the physical and divine planes, and also in the context of the sacrifice, they with concentrated minds know me even at the time of death.

7.30.author: Swami Sivananda
7.30.text: Those who know Me with the Adhibhuta (pertaining to the elements), Adhidaiva (pertaining to the gods), and the Adhiyajna (pertaining to the sacrifice) know Me even at the time of death, remaining steadfast in mind.

7.30.author: Shri Purohit Swami
7.30.text: Those who see Me in the life of the world, in the universal sacrifice, and as pure Divinity, keeping their minds steady, they live in Me even in the hour of death's approach.
